name: Capital Spending Decisions
title: Capital Spending Decisions
answer: Capital spending decisions in an AI context cover how a company chooses where to commit money for compute, data, talent and tooling, and how those choices are justified to a board or finance committee. The scope runs from small software subscriptions up to multi year data centre and chip commitments, and it includes the decision to defer, lease or buy. It sits inside forecasting and planning because every commitment changes the cash profile and the depreciation schedule that later forecasts must carry.

sections.body: Capital spending decisions in an AI context cover how a company chooses where to commit money for compute, data, talent and tooling, and how those choices are justified to a board or finance committee. The scope runs from small software subscriptions up to multi year data centre and chip commitments, and it includes the decision to defer, lease or buy. It sits inside forecasting and planning because every commitment changes the cash profile and the depreciation schedule that later forecasts must carry.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on the same planning stack a finance team already uses, typically an ERP or EPM system for budgets and commitments, a data warehouse for actual spend, and spreadsheets or planning tools for scenarios. AI specific inputs are added on top, such as cloud usage bills, GPU reservation contracts and vendor quotes, which often arrive in different formats and cadences.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Analysts build a base case from historical spend, then layer scenarios for demand, utilisation and price changes, testing how each assumption moves the payback period. They separate operating spend from capital spend, check whether a commitment can be scaled down, and compare owned capacity against rented capacity over the same horizon. Sensitivity tables and break even points are the usual outputs, and they are refreshed as vendor pricing and internal usage data change.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Approval usually follows a delegation of authority, with thresholds that decide whether a purchase needs a manager, a finance committee or the board. Documentation matters, so the assumptions, the alternatives considered and the reason for the chosen option are recorded for audit and for later review against actual results.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Expect more frequent re forecasting as hardware prices, model efficiency and vendor terms shift within a single budget year. Finance teams are moving toward continuous spend monitoring rather than annual capital plans, with usage data feeding the model directly. The harder problem is attributing value, since AI spend often lands in shared infrastructure and its returns show up in many parts of the business rather than one line item.
